Kenopsia

The eerie feeling of being somewhere that’s usually busy when everyone is gone.

  • Emotions
  • Liminal Spaces
  • Vocabulary

Context

John Koenig coined the word for The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows. The feeling often comes from the contrast between what a place looks like and what you expect it to sound or feel like when it’s full of people.

A liminal space describes the setting or the sense of being in between. Kenopsia names a feeling the setting can evoke. The atmosphere can carry a feeling of forlornness.

Examples

  • “After the last class left, the stillness of the school hallway gave me a feeling of kenopsia.”
